revisionHistory.summary: Factual corrections after a second backend audit, plus the architectural contracts the first revision left undefined.
factualCorrections: fetchOptionChainNested does NOT use the global ttFetch — it performs a route-local fetch with injected getAccessToken, route-local timeout and deadline, and route-local structured error classification. ttFetch removed from its dependency list.

OptionChainCache does NOT use createRequestCoalescer — it owns its own `pending` Map and `coalesce()` method. createRequestCoalescer is used by server.js for marketMetricsCache and candlesResponseCache, and is AVAILABLE (not yet used) for stress-run single-flight.
OptionChainCache stale-while-revalidate uses a background revalidation PROMISE gated on `softExpired`; there is no dedicated timer. The phrase 'background revalidation timer' was wrong.

Exact-contract hydration does NOT go through the option chain. The production enriched path builds the canonical symbol, deduplicates, and reads the DXLink caches by exact symbol with ZERO option-chain access. The nested chain is a discovery/browsing owner, not a hydration owner.
The market-context snapshot must stay portfolio-agnostic and is REUSE, not EXTEND. The stress-run snapshot is a separate NEW responsibility.

Backend Greeks are RAW dxFeed event values; the source states 'volatility is the fractional IV (e.g. 0.23) — NEVER multiply it by 100'. The previous 'per share' claim was an inference, not a proven provider contract.
Frontend Portfolio helpers are NOT callable from the backend. Ownership is now stated per execution tier with an explicit parity contract.
serverJsLines corrected from 18939 (a route line number) to the real 19364; routeCount corrected from 95 to 93.
The base commit advanced: PR #357 was merged into dev-clean after revision 1.0.0 was cut. Rebased and every hash re-derived.

The target backend replaced it (PR #210) with a deferred, BATCHED, BOUNDED phase: runUnderlyingLastCloseFallbacks with a 2-worker pool, a 450ms per-symbol timeout and a 1200ms total budget, plus underlyingLastCloseFallbackDiagnostics.
The live-refresh IVR phase is also bounded on the target backend (PR #211) with its own ivrDiagnostics, which the previous reactivity audit did not mention.

Facts, not implementations, are recorded here; no runtime code is copied.

facts.evidence: NOT call the global ttFetch(). Instead it performs its own fetch so the route
facts.detail: The module header states the design explicitly. With comments stripped the module contains ZERO ttFetch call sites and ZERO imports. The provider call is `fetchImpl(url, {...})`, where `fetchImpl = fetch` is an injectable parameter.

facts.claim: fetchOptionChainNested receives getAccessToken as an injected dependency
facts.evidence: getAccessToken is injected (it is shared, read-only auth) so the

facts.detail: 16000ms bounds the upstream provider fetch; 18500ms bounds the whole route including auth, body read, parse and validation, and must stay below the frontend's ~20000ms ttCall budget.

facts.claim: fetchOptionChainNested classifies errors route-locally
facts.detail: Codes are timeout | auth | not_found | malformed | upstream. The typed error is kept internal to this route family so nothing globally starts inspecting err.code / err.status.

facts.detail: lookup() classifies an entry as miss | fresh | stale and flags `softExpired` when a background revalidation is due. The revalidation is a background promise started by the route on a soft-expired hit, not a scheduled timer. The module contains zero setTimeout and zero setInterval calls.

facts.detail: These are its only production consumers. It is therefore AVAILABLE — an audited, tested TTL micro-cache plus single-flight owner — for the future stress-run single-flight, but it is NOT today the option-chain cache's coalescer.

facts.detail: Inside POST /portfolio/live-refresh each underlying resolves to { bid, ask, last, price, mark, source, updatedAt, isStale, quoteAgeMs, quoteFreshness, quoteUsableForPortfolioValuation, fallbackLastClose, errors } with source in DXLINK | CACHED_DXLINK | LAST_CLOSE | UNKNOWN and freshness in live | usable_recent_stale | last_close | missing. facts.evidence: function approxDelta(type, spot, strike, ivDecimal, dteDays) {
facts.detail: approxDelta is a route-local closure inside GET /eic/legs/:symbol. It is unexported and untested, has zero call sites, and its body reads the undefined identifier `dteDay` while its parameter is `dteDays`, so invoking it would throw ReferenceError. facts.claim: the target backend resolves missing underlying prices through a deferred, batched, bounded fallback phase
facts.detail: Quotes are classified first into underlyingFallbackNeeded (11432, 11485); runUnderlyingLastCloseFallbacks is then invoked ONCE for the whole batch (11489) and the per-symbol loop reads the precomputed underlyingLastCloseBySymbol map (11505). The phase runs a worker pool of UNDERLYING_LAST_CLOSE_FALLBACK_CONCURRENCY = 2, with a per-symbol timeout of 450ms raced against the work, and breaks out entirely once UNDERLYING_LAST_CLOSE_FALLBACK_TOTAL_BUDGET_MS = 1200 is exhausted. Any symbol never reached is recorded as timed out rather than left undefined.
facts.supersedes: main@6eebb99 awaited getUnderlyingLastClose(sym) INLINE inside the per-symbol loop (main server.js:11242) — serial and unbounded. Revisions 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 described that behaviour as current; it is not, on the target backend.

facts.claim: the bounded fallback publishes its own diagnostics
facts.detail: underlyingLastCloseFallbackDiagnostics carries attemptedSymbols, resolvedSymbols, timedOutSymbols, missingSymbols, concurrency, perSymbolTimeoutMs, totalBudgetMs and durationMs, and the phase logs a start line and a summary line. A stress run reusing this owner inherits ready-made per-symbol provenance and status.

facts.claim: the target backend bounds the live-refresh IVR phase and reports its own diagnostics
facts.detail: PR #211 bounded the IVR phase: unresolved symbols are marked timed out via markIvrTimeout rather than allowed to extend the request, and ivrDiagnostics publishes resolvedSymbols, missingSymbols, timedOutSymbols, cacheUsed and durationMs.

facts.claim: market-metrics reads are served through the createRequestCoalescer-backed marketMetricsCache

facts.detail: getMarketMetricsItemCached is the single read path for Tastytrade market-metrics; live-refresh warms it (11269) and then awaits it inside the bounded IVR phase (11295). This is a real production consumer of createRequestCoalescer, alongside candlesResponseCache — further evidence that the option-chain cache's single-flight is a DIFFERENT owner.

portfolioReactivityAudit.question: Why is the current Portfolio sufficiently reactive?
portfolioReactivityAudit.answerBasis: measured from the source of the backend actually targeted (dev-4h-backend@25dd8424), not from visual perception and not from main
portfolioReactivityAudit.supersedes: Revisions 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 answered this against main@6eebb99, where the underlying-price fallback was a serial, unbounded inline await. That is NOT the behaviour of the target backend.

requestsPerRefreshCycle.detail: POST /portfolio/live-refresh (server.js:11029-13186) carries ALL positions, ALL underlying symbols and ALL option streamer symbols in one body and returns underlyings + options + positions in one response.
requestsPerRefreshCycle.technicalRefresh: 0 or 1, plus at most 1 targeted retry for missing tickers

whyItIsFast: The backend holds a single persistent DXLink WebSocket and serves quotes/Greeks from in-memory Maps (quoteCache:722, greeksCache:726, optionQuoteCache:732) rather than fetching per request.
Option hydration is BY EXACT SYMBOL with Set-based dedupe — both Portfolio routes contain ZERO option-chain access of any kind, measured over their exact boundaries.

The underlying-price fallback is DEFERRED, BATCHED and BOUNDED (PR #210): symbols are collected into underlyingFallbackNeeded, then runUnderlyingLastCloseFallbacks (11372) runs once with a 2-worker pool, a 450ms per-symbol timeout and a 1200ms TOTAL budget. A slow or dead provider costs the request at most 1.2s regardless of portfolio size — it cannot serialise into an unbounded stall.
The IVR phase is bounded too (PR #211): unresolved symbols are marked timed out via markIvrTimeout instead of extending the request, with ivrDiagnostics published.
market-metrics reads are coalesced and TTL-cached through getMarketMetricsItemCached over marketMetricsCache (3430/3439), so N positions on the same underlying cost one upstream call.
Underlying symbols are deduplicated into a Set before subscribing, so N legs on the same contract cost one subscription.
The whole route runs under an explicit server budget with per-phase timings, so a slow phase degrades rather than blocking.
Log throttling and greeks-log capping (PR #213/#214) plus the /market/quotes circuit breaker (PR #209) stop a degraded upstream from turning into a log storm that slows the process itself.
All portfolio Greek aggregation, beta-weighted delta and risk metrics are pure in-memory frontend functions over data already in hand.
A frontend storm circuit breaker (_backendCircuitOpen) suppresses per-symbol live fan-out entirely while the backend is unreachable.
portfolioReactivityAudit.implicationForStress: The stress endpoint MUST reproduce this shape: ONE batch request carrying every scenario, hydrating each exact contract at most once per run BY EXACT SYMBOL, with the option chain used only for discovery, and with every remaining provider fallback given an explicit concurrency limit, per-item timeout and total budget in the manner of runUnderlyingLastCloseFallbacks. Copying the bounded-fallback SHAPE is required; copying its CODE is forbidden (PST-REUSE-003).

boundedFallbackReferenceParameters.note: Recorded as the AUDITED values of the reused owner, not as approved stress thresholds. Stress budgets must be derived from the PR 2 benchmarks (PST-PERF-003).

contracts.title: Inventory before design
contracts.text: Every future responsibility MUST appear in the Reuse Manifest before it is assigned to a module.

contracts.title: One canonical owner per responsibility per execution tier
contracts.text: Every responsibility MUST have exactly one canonical owner PER EXECUTION TIER (frontend presentation tier, backend execution tier). A responsibility owned in both tiers MUST declare both owners explicitly and MUST be covered by a parity contract; it MUST NOT be claimed that a frontend declaration inside index.html is directly callable from the backend. Within a single tier, two implementations of the same responsibility remain forbidden.

contracts.title: No copied implementation
contracts.text: An existing function MUST NOT be copied, transcribed or rewritten under a new name, within a tier or across tiers. Cross-tier agreement MUST be achieved by a parity contract over shared fixtures, not by physical duplication.

contracts.title: Thin delegation only
contracts.text: A new adapter MAY delegate to an existing owner, but MUST NOT re-transcribe its formulas, normalization or fallbacks.

contracts.title: No parallel caches
contracts.text: No parallel cache MUST be introduced for data already owned by Portfolio, DXLink, the option-chain cache, the candle store or market context.

contracts.title: No parallel market-data path
contracts.text: No second path MUST be introduced for SPY, VIX, option quotes, option Greeks, beta or underlying spot.

contracts.title: Extension before replacement
contracts.text: When a partial owner exists, the default decision MUST be EXTEND, not NEW.

contracts.title: Existing tests remain authoritative
contracts.text: Future implementations MUST continue to pass the tests of every reused owner.

contracts.title: No ownership by filename assumption
contracts.text: The name of a new file MUST NOT be decided before the ownership audit.

contracts.title: Reuse evidence
contracts.text: Every REUSE or EXTEND decision MUST state definition, callers, tests, units, dependencies and the reason for the choice.

contracts.title: No third coalescing implementation
contracts.text: Single-flight behaviour MUST reuse an existing owner. OptionChainCache.coalesce owns option-chain single-flight; createRequestCoalescer owns TTL micro-cache single-flight and is available for stress runs. A third coalescing implementation MUST NOT be introduced.

contracts.title: Canonical transport
contracts.text: The future Stress Test client MUST use the existing canonical backend transport (ttCall).

contracts.title: No new direct fetch
contracts.text: The Stress Test client MUST NOT contain a new direct fetch when ttCall or the canonical client can perform the request.

contracts.title: Reuse the transport policy
contracts.text: Authentication, API key, session ID, timeout policy, JSON parsing and error classification MUST be reused.

contracts.title: Budget as owner extension
contracts.text: Any different timeout budget MUST be implemented as an explicit extension of the transport owner, never as a parallel client.

contracts.title: Run-authoritative SPY owner
contracts.text: The run's SPY price MUST be frozen by the BACKEND Stress Engine using the existing backend underlying spot owner and the same market-data snapshot as the rest of the run. The contract MUST NOT require the backend to call a frontend function. The frontend resolver remains the canonical owner for Portfolio display and optional preflight comparison.

contracts.title: No second SPY resolver
contracts.text: A second SPY resolver MUST NOT be created in either tier.

contracts.title: Frozen SPY snapshot fields
contracts.text: A run MUST freeze spySnapshotPrice, spyPriceSource, spyPriceTimestamp and snapshotCreatedAt, and the response MUST report them.

contracts.title: Percentage shock
contracts.text: stressedSpyPrice = spySnapshotPrice x (1 + spyReturn).

contracts.title: Absolute target
contracts.text: impliedSpyReturn = targetSpyPrice / spySnapshotPrice - 1.

contracts.title: Missing SPY never becomes zero
contracts.text: A missing or stale SPY price MUST produce DEGRADED or UNAVAILABLE, never zero.

contracts.title: One run, one frozen SPY source
contracts.text: A run MUST have exactly one frozen SPY source. The frontend MUST display the returned triple and MAY compare it with the price Portfolio already shows, but MUST NOT run a second resolver for the same run and MUST NOT substitute its own value after the run has started.

contracts.title: Real selected portfolio
contracts.text: The baseline MUST be the portfolio actually selected.

contracts.title: Canonical scope helpers per tier
contracts.text: The canonical scope and active-leg filtering owners OF THE EXECUTING TIER MUST be reused. The backend Stress Engine MUST use the backend owners; it MUST NOT transcribe the frontend helpers.

contracts.title: Terminal legs contribute zero
contracts.text: Closed, rolled, terminal and quantity-zero legs MUST contribute zero.

contracts.title: Other portfolios excluded
contracts.text: Positions belonging to other portfolios MUST be excluded.

contracts.title: Immutable input
contracts.text: The Actual Portfolio input MUST be immutable.

contracts.title: No second Portfolio rule set
contracts.text: A second, Stress-Test-specific set of Portfolio rules MUST NOT be created in either tier.

contracts.title: Cross-tier scope agreement
contracts.text: The frontend and backend owners MUST agree, on the same fixture, about: trade open/closed, leg active/terminal, rolled, assigned, exercised, expired, partial close, and residual quantity zero versus non-zero.

contracts.title: Semantic parity, not physical duplication
contracts.text: The frontend implementation MUST NOT be copied into the backend word for word when the backend already has its own owner. The objective is semantic parity.

contracts.title: Divergence fails the run
contracts.text: A divergence between the backend stress scope and the Portfolio UI scope MUST make the run unavailable and MUST produce diagnostics. It MUST NOT be tolerated silently.

contracts.title: Shared fixtures
contracts.text: Parity fixtures MUST be shared or generated from a common manifest, so the two tiers cannot drift behind two independent sets of expected values.

contracts.title: Taxonomy changes update both tiers
contracts.text: Any future change to the status taxonomy MUST update both owners and the parity tests in the same change.

contracts.title: Canonical builder
contracts.text: The backend MUST reuse the existing canonical option-symbol builder.

contracts.title: No second formatter
contracts.text: A second formatter for root, expiry, type or strike MUST NOT be created.

contracts.title: Dotted roots preserved
contracts.text: Dotted roots such as BRK.B MUST preserve canonical semantics.

contracts.title: Exact contract identity
contracts.text: The exact contract MUST be identified by underlying, expiration, strike and PUT/CALL.

contracts.title: No nearest substitution
contracts.text: A contract MUST NOT be substituted with the nearest strike or the nearest expiry.

contracts.title: Exact-symbol hydration is the primary path
contracts.text: When underlying, expiration, strike and PUT/CALL are already known, the backend MUST hydrate the contract by: building the exact canonical symbol via the canonical builder; deduplicating by canonical symbol; reading the canonical optionQuoteCache and greeksCache directly; applying the same freshness and missing-reason rules the Portfolio enriched path already uses; optionally requesting or warming that single exact symbol through the existing DXLink orchestration; and returning quote, Greeks, provenance and timestamps. The nested option chain MUST NOT be on this path.

contracts.title: Nested chain is discovery and fallback
contracts.text: The nested option chain MUST be used only to populate expiration and strike selectors, to browse the chain, to confirm contract availability when needed, as a diagnostic fallback when the exact canonical symbol cannot be validated, and to retrieve metadata unobtainable from the exact-symbol path.

contracts.title: Contract not found
contracts.text: A contract that cannot be found MUST yield UNAVAILABLE — exact contract not found.

contracts.title: One hydration per contract per run
contracts.text: Each exact contract MUST be hydrated at most once per run, deduplicated by canonical symbol. Two identical legs MUST cause exactly one hydration.

contracts.title: At most one chain fetch per underlying
contracts.text: When the nested chain is genuinely required, it MUST be fetched at most once per underlying per run, through the existing chain cache and its coalescer. A chain fetch per scenario, per cell, or per already-identified leg is forbidden.

contracts.title: No mandatory chain when the exact symbol resolves
contracts.text: A chain fetch MUST NOT be required when the exact symbol's quote and Greeks are already available. An unavailable or failing chain MUST NOT make an exact symbol UNAVAILABLE when the DXLink caches already hold its data.

contracts.title: Hydration provenance
contracts.text: Every hydrated leg MUST report which path resolved it (exact_symbol_cache | exact_symbol_warmed | chain_confirmed | unresolved), together with provenance, timestamps and, when unresolved, a missing reason.

contracts.title: Canonical current spot
contracts.text: Every symbol MUST start from the current spot obtained from the canonical owners the Portfolio already uses. No second spot resolver MUST be created.

contracts.title: Manual symbol override
contracts.text: The user MAY set the percentage shock of an individual underlying directly. A manual override MUST take precedence over any beta-derived shock and MUST be visible in the diagnostics.

contracts.title: Downside beta
contracts.text: When a measured and documented downside beta exists, it MAY be used to derive a symbol's shock from SPY's. A downside beta MUST NOT be invented. No downside beta exists in either repository at the audited commit.

contracts.title: Ordinary beta fallback
contracts.text: When only ordinary beta exists it MAY be used as a fallback, but it MUST NOT be called downside beta, its source MUST be shown, the result MUST be at least DEGRADED, and a manual override MUST remain possible.

contracts.title: Return formula
contracts.text: symbolStressReturn = manualSymbolReturn, or else betaShockFactor x spyReturn + idiosyncraticReturnOverride. betaShockFactor MUST declare its source; idiosyncraticReturnOverride MUST have an explicit, non-hidden default; and a missing input MUST NOT silently become zero.

contracts.title: Stressed spot
contracts.text: stressedSpot = currentSpot x (1 + symbolStressReturn). The stressed spot MUST be finite and strictly greater than zero, and MUST carry a source and a confidence/status.

contracts.title: Missing mapping
contracts.text: When no manual override, no downside beta, no approved ordinary beta and no explicitly configured fallback exists, the position MUST be UNAVAILABLE. It MUST NOT be assumed to move with SPY and MUST NOT be assigned beta 1.

contracts.title: Signed shares
contracts.text: Equities and ETFs MUST use a signed share quantity: signedShares > 0 for LONG, signedShares < 0 for SHORT. The option contract multiplier MUST NOT be applied to them.

contracts.title: Equity stress P&L
contracts.text: equityStressPnl = (stressedSpot - currentSpot) x signedShares.

contracts.title: Reconciliation
contracts.text: The sum of optionLegStressPnl and equityStressPnl MUST reconcile exactly to the Portfolio Stress P&L, within the documented tolerance.

contracts.title: One snapshot per run
contracts.text: Actual, Overlay, Proposed and Difference MUST be computed from the same frozen stress-run snapshot.

contracts.title: Snapshot identity fields
contracts.text: A stress-run snapshot MUST carry snapshotId, snapshotCreatedAt, modelVersion, activePortfolioId, portfolioRevision, positionsHash, spySnapshotPrice, spyPriceSource, spyPriceTimestamp, vixCurrent, vixSource, vixTimestamp, underlyingPrices, optionQuotes, impliedVolatilities, greeks, overlayHash, scenarioHash and marketDataAsOf.

contracts.title: Invalidation
contracts.text: A run MUST be invalidated when the portfolio, a real position, a residual quantity, SPY, VIX, the scenario, the overlay, a strike, an expiry, a side, a contract count, the entry method or the model version changes.

contracts.title: Stale result is announced
contracts.text: An invalidated result MUST be shown as INPUTS CHANGED — RERUN REQUIRED and MUST NOT be silently recomputed or silently displayed as current.

contracts.title: Market context stays portfolio-agnostic
contracts.text: The generic market-context snapshot MUST NOT be extended with portfolio identity, positions hash, overlay hash, scenario hash or any stress-run identity. It is reused as a market-data input only.

contracts.title: Stress-run snapshot composes, never duplicates
contracts.text: The stress-run snapshot builder MUST compose the existing portfolio, market-data, SPY, VIX, spot, quote and Greeks owners without duplicating any of their sources. An overlay change MUST invalidate the run without invalidating the global market-context cache.

contracts.title: Additive overlay
contracts.text: Proposed = Actual + Overlay. Proposed = Overlay is forbidden.

contracts.title: Leg definition
contracts.text: Every hypothetical leg MUST carry underlying, expiration, strike, optionType, side, contracts and contractMultiplier.

contracts.title: Ephemeral and non-persistent
contracts.text: The overlay MUST NOT modify Portfolio, Journal, the backend trade store, localStorage, orders, real quantities, real legs or any persistent cache.

contracts.title: Signed contracts
contracts.text: signedContracts > 0 for LONG and < 0 for SHORT, applied exactly once together with contractMultiplier.

contracts.title: Entry methods
contracts.text: MARK, MID, BID, ASK and MANUAL MUST be supported and the chosen method MUST be reported with the resulting estimatedEntryPrice, its source and its timestamp.

contracts.title: No double counting
contracts.text: A debit MUST NOT be counted twice, and a credit MUST NOT be declared as initial profit.

contracts.title: Overlay P&L formula
contracts.text: hypotheticalLegStressPnl = (stressedMark - estimatedEntryPrice) x signedContracts x contractMultiplier.

contracts.title: Independent SPY and VIX inputs
contracts.text: spyReturn (or targetSpyPrice) and vixTarget (or vixChangePct) are distinct inputs. A VIX level MUST NOT automatically imply a single SPY move.

contracts.title: Scenario fields
contracts.text: Every scenario MUST specify spyReturn or targetSpyPrice, vixCurrent, vixTarget or vixChangePct, horizonDays and ivShockMethod.

contracts.title: Presets are illustrative
contracts.text: PURE_VOLATILITY, CORRECTION, STRESS, CRASH and CUSTOM MUST be presented as illustrative hypotheses, never as forecasts.

contracts.title: IV shock methods
contracts.text: DIRECT_IV_SHOCK and VIX_PROXY MUST both be supported and clearly distinguished.

contracts.title: Relative vs points
contracts.text: A relative IV shock and a volatility-points shock MUST be distinct, explicitly labelled modes.

contracts.title: No invented calibration
contracts.text: Historical volatility betas MUST NOT be invented. Without a real calibration the coefficient MUST be configurable, carry provenance, mark the result DEGRADED and allow a manual override.

contracts.title: No hidden clamps
contracts.text: No hidden clamp MUST be applied to a shocked implied volatility. Any bound MUST be declared and reported.

contracts.title: Declared limitations
contracts.text: Unsupported skew and term-structure behaviour MUST be declared as explicit limitations.

contracts.title: Engine canonical units
contracts.text: The pricing and scenario engines MUST operate on their own canonical mathematical units, declared in the units block, and MUST record the unit of every input they consume.

contracts.title: No presentation transform as engine input
contracts.text: normalizeGreekPoints MUST NOT be applied to any pricing or scenario engine input. It is a presentation and compatibility transform belonging to the current Portfolio.

contracts.title: Raw and display outputs are distinct
contracts.text: Raw engine outputs and display outputs MUST be distinct fields. A display transform MUST NOT overwrite the raw value.

contracts.title: Actual and Overlay share units
contracts.text: Actual and Overlay MUST be compared in the same raw units. Mixing a raw Greek with a points-normalized Greek is forbidden.

contracts.title: No magnitude heuristics on engine inputs
contracts.text: No heuristic based on the magnitude of a value MUST alter an engine input. Provider units MUST be established by contract, not inferred from how large a number looks.

contracts.title: Full repricing
contracts.text: The primary pricing MUST be a full repricing. Vega x delta-IV MUST NOT be the primary method; it MAY appear only as secondary diagnostics.

contracts.title: Pricing inputs
contracts.text: Pricing MUST take spot, strike, timeToExpiry, impliedVolatility, riskFreeRate, dividendYield, optionType and exerciseStyle.

contracts.title: American exercise
contracts.text: American-style options MUST support early exercise.

contracts.title: Anchored repricing
contracts.text: stressedMark = currentMarketMark + stressedTheoreticalValue - baseTheoreticalValue.

contracts.title: Pricing ownership
contracts.text: The pricing engine MAY be classified NEW only after the absence proof. If any pricing owner is found it MUST be REUSE or EXTEND.

contracts.title: Pricing is backend-owned
contracts.text: No pricing formula MUST exist in the frontend, and none MUST exist in index.html.

contracts.title: No hidden rate or yield defaults
contracts.text: riskFreeRate and dividendYield MUST NOT have hidden defaults. A manual configuration MUST carry provenance, and a declared default MUST produce at least DEGRADED.

contracts.title: Absent rate or yield may make a leg unavailable
contracts.text: When the selected pricing model requires a rate or a dividend yield that cannot be sourced or configured, the affected leg MUST be UNAVAILABLE rather than priced on an invented input.

contracts.title: Four result sets
contracts.text: The backend MUST produce actualResult, overlayResult, proposedResult and differenceResult.

contracts.title: Additivity
contracts.text: proposedStressPnl = actualStressPnl + overlayStressPnl within a documented tolerance.

contracts.title: Incremental effect
contracts.text: incrementalEffect = proposedStressPnl - actualStressPnl.

contracts.title: Shared inputs
contracts.text: Actual and Proposed MUST use the same SPY, VIX, scenario, horizon, model, snapshot, stressed spots and sources.

contracts.title: Backend batch matrix
contracts.text: The numerical matrix MUST be computed by the backend in a single batch request containing every scenario.

contracts.title: Frontend renders only
contracts.text: The visual scenario grid MUST remain frontend-owned and MUST NOT compute stress values.

contracts.title: Minimum grid
contracts.text: The minimum matrix is SPY 0%, -5%, -10%, -15%, -20% by VIX current, +50%, +100%, +200%.

contracts.title: Cell fields
contracts.text: Each cell MUST carry scenarioId, spyReturn, stressedSpyPrice, vixTarget, actualStressPnl, proposedStressPnl, difference, actualStressPnlPctNlv, proposedStressPnlPctNlv and status.

contracts.title: No per-cell work
contracts.text: One request per cell, a full pricing loop in the renderer, a fetch per leg per scenario and an option-chain fetch per cell are all forbidden.

contracts.title: Benchmarks required
contracts.text: Benchmarks MUST be defined for 10, 30, 60 and 100 legs against 20 scenarios, measuring elapsed time, CPU, memory, pricing count, provider calls, cache hits, coalesced requests, request bytes, response bytes, cold cache, warm cache, Actual only, Actual + Overlay and the full matrix.

contracts.title: No N+1
contracts.text: No request per position, per leg per scenario or per cell MUST exist, and no option-chain request or quote hydration MUST be repeated for the same exact contract within a run.

contracts.title: Limits derive from measurement
contracts.text: Final performance limits MUST be derived from the benchmarks, not asserted in advance.

contracts.title: Three statuses
contracts.text: Every result MUST carry status VALID, DEGRADED or UNAVAILABLE.

contracts.title: Missing never becomes a silent default
contracts.text: A missing input MUST NOT be converted into zero, and MUST NOT be converted into any other silent default such as a quantity of one or a beta of one.

contracts.title: No silent exclusion
contracts.text: An unavailable leg MUST NOT be silently included or silently dropped.

contracts.title: Incomplete Proposed is not VALID
contracts.text: An incomplete Proposed result MUST NOT be reported as VALID.

contracts.title: Coverage reporting
contracts.text: Legs requested, legs evaluated, legs excluded, reasons, excluded value, sources, timestamps and fallbacks MUST be reported.

contracts.title: No new stress surface and no new duplicate owner in the monolith
contracts.text: index.html MUST NOT receive new Stress-Test-specific logic, a second implementation of an existing owner, new pricing formulas, a scenario engine, a matrix engine, overlay calculations, stress-run state, a stress renderer, a stress cache, stress data-quality rules or stress contract constants. Audited legacy owners already present in index.html are tolerated, remain out of scope for this PR, and their eventual extraction requires a separate audit-and-extraction PR.

contracts.title: Permitted monolith additions
contracts.text: Future runtime PRs MAY add to index.html only a stylesheet link, a script tag, a STRESS TEST navigation entry, an empty mount point and a minimal bootstrap call site.

contracts.title: Specification PR is inert
contracts.text: This specification PR MUST NOT modify index.html, js/** or css/**, MUST NOT add an endpoint, MUST NOT implement behaviour, MUST NOT add persistence and MUST NOT place an order.

contracts.title: Freeze before calculation
contracts.text: Every market input MUST be read and copied into the stress-run snapshot BEFORE any scenario calculation begins. No scenario, cell or leg may be evaluated against a value that was not already frozen.

contracts.title: No reread during the matrix
contracts.text: The pricing engine and the matrix engine MUST NOT reread the quote cache, the Greeks cache, SPY, VIX, underlying prices or Portfolio state while computing cells. All cells MUST use the same frozen values.

contracts.title: Snapshot assembly interval
contracts.text: The snapshot MUST report snapshotStartedAt, snapshotCompletedAt and snapshotAssemblyMs.

contracts.title: Per-input timestamp and age
contracts.text: Every input MUST report source, asOf, ageMs, freshness and status. This applies to SPY, VIX, underlying prices, option quotes, implied volatilities, Greeks, beta and NLV.

contracts.title: Cross-input skew
contracts.text: The snapshot MUST compute oldestInputAsOf, newestInputAsOf, maxCrossInputSkewMs and maxInputAgeMs.

contracts.title: Explicit temporal policy
contracts.text: Temporal thresholds MUST derive from the declared freshness policy and the PR 2 benchmarks. No threshold may be hidden. An input beyond threshold MUST produce DEGRADED or UNAVAILABLE according to a declared rule.

contracts.title: Same snapshot for Actual and Proposed
contracts.text: Actual, Overlay, Proposed and Difference MUST use the same snapshot id, the same prices, the same timestamps, the same implied volatilities, the same Greeks, the same beta and the same NLV. Adding or editing the Overlay MUST NOT cause a new market read.

underlyingShockModel.formula: symbolStressReturn = manualSymbolReturn OR (betaShockFactor x spyReturn + idiosyncraticReturnOverride)
underlyingShockModel.idiosyncraticReturnOverrideNote: The default is zero and it is DECLARED here, so it is an explicit modelling choice rather than a hidden fallback, and it MUST be reported in the per-symbol diagnostics whenever applied. This is distinct from PST-DATA-002, which forbids turning a MISSING input into a silent default: a missing beta or a missing mapping never becomes zero or one, it becomes UNAVAILABLE.

stressedSpot can never be <= 0
Actual and Proposed use the same stressed spot for the same symbol
position ordering does not change any result

100 shares short

shares plus a protective put reconcile
no multiplier of 100 is applied to shares

forbidden: a full pricing loop in the renderer
a fetch per leg per scenario

resolvedDecisions.question: Does the stress request pass a portfolioId, or a full client-side position snapshot?
resolvedDecisions.resolution: portfolioId + portfolioRevision. The backend hydrates server-side via buildPortfolioPositionsFromJournal, which POST /portfolio/:portfolioId/positions/enriched already does in production. buildPortfolioPositionsFromPayload stays as the audited fallback and taking it must be reported.

resolvedDecisions.question: Do stress inputs and outputs use raw Greeks or points-normalized values?
resolvedDecisions.resolution: RAW. The engine operates on its own canonical units and MUST NOT consume normalizeGreekPoints output. That transform stays a presentation/compatibility concern of the current Portfolio. Raw and display outputs are distinct fields, Actual and Overlay are compared in the same raw units, and no magnitude heuristic may alter an engine input.

resolvedDecisions.question: Which end of the system freezes the SPY triple for a run?
resolvedDecisions.resolution: THE BACKEND. Pricing and the matrix are backend-owned and the backend cannot call a frontend function, so the run freezes SPY through the existing backend underlying spot owner and the run's own market-data snapshot, and returns spySnapshotPrice, spyPriceSource and spyPriceTimestamp. The frontend displays that triple, may compare it with what Portfolio already shows, and must not run a second resolver or substitute a value after the run starts.

resolvedDecisions.question: What is the primary hydration path for an exactly-identified hypothetical contract?
resolvedDecisions.resolution: EXACT-SYMBOL. Build the canonical symbol, deduplicate, read optionQuoteCache and greeksCache directly, reuse the enriched path's freshness and missing-reason rules, optionally warm that single symbol through existing DXLink orchestration. The nested chain is discovery and fallback only, and an unavailable chain must not make an exact symbol unavailable when the caches already hold its data.

resolvedDecisions.question: Who owns the stress-run snapshot?
resolvedDecisions.resolution: A NEW stress-run snapshot builder inside the Stress Engine, which COMPOSES the existing owners. The generic market-context snapshot stays portfolio-agnostic and is reused unmodified.

resolvedDecisions.question: How do non-SPY underlyings get their stressed spot?
resolvedDecisions.resolution: Through an explicit mapping with declared precedence: manual override, then a real downside beta, then ordinary beta as a DEGRADED fallback, otherwise UNAVAILABLE. No downside beta exists at the audited commit, ordinary beta must never be relabelled as downside beta, and a missing mapping never becomes beta 1.

resolvedDecisions.question: How is equity/ETF stress P&L computed?
resolvedDecisions.resolution: equityStressPnl = (stressedSpot - currentSpot) x signedShares, with signed SHARES and no option contract multiplier, reconciling with the option-leg P&L into the Portfolio Stress P&L.

resolvedDecisions.question: How do the frontend and backend Portfolio rules stay in agreement?
resolvedDecisions.resolution: Each tier keeps its own canonical owner; agreement is enforced by a cross-tier parity contract over shared fixtures, and a divergence makes the run unavailable rather than being tolerated.

openDecisions.question: What is the exact VIX-to-IV conversion for VIX_PROXY?
openDecisions.evidence: The backend VIX family is delivered in index points (18.0 means 18), while option implied volatilities are decimals (0.18). No conversion and no volatility-beta calibration exists anywhere in either repository.
openDecisions.implication: Any VIX_PROXY implementation without a stated conversion and a real calibration must be DEGRADED with a configurable coefficient.

openDecisions.question: What does the threshold 'Vega LP / |Vega SP| > 30' mean?
openDecisions.evidence: Recorded verbatim from the requesting specification. It is NOT reinterpreted as 30% by this document.
openDecisions.implication: The ratio could be a pure ratio of 30, a percentage of 30%, or a differently-scaled comparison. Choosing one silently would encode an unapproved threshold.
openDecisions.status: OPEN — SEMANTICS UNDECIDED, MUST NOT BE AUTO-INTERPRETED
openDecisions.mustResolveBefore: any PR that surfaces this ratio

openDecisions.question: Which provider supplies riskFreeRate and dividendYield?
openDecisions.evidence: Neither value exists as a data source in either repository. riskFreeRate, risk-free and discount factor return zero matches; the only DividendYield is a display-only Alpha Vantage fundamental at index.html:15470.
openDecisions.implication: Until a real provider exists these are configuration inputs, not data. PST-PRICING-007 already forbids hidden defaults, requires provenance on a manual configuration, and forces at least DEGRADED on a declared default; PST-PRICING-008 already makes a leg UNAVAILABLE when the selected model needs a value that cannot be sourced or configured. Only the choice of provider remains open.
openDecisions.mustResolveBefore: shipping a model that requires them

openDecisions.question: Which provider supplies NLV for the %NLV outputs?
openDecisions.evidence: netLiq is fetched from GET /account/:number/balances and rendered at index.html:3749. It is not threaded into any risk computation today.
openDecisions.implication: actualStressPnlPctNlv and proposedStressPnlPctNlv require an explicit NLV input with its own source and timestamp, or they are UNAVAILABLE. The same no-hidden-default discipline as PST-PRICING-007 applies.

openDecisions.question: What is the documented additivity tolerance for PST-RESULT-002 and PST-EQUITY-003?
openDecisions.evidence: No tolerance is established because no pricing implementation exists yet to measure floating-point drift against.
openDecisions.implication: PR 2 must derive the tolerance from measured behaviour and record it here, rather than asserting one now.

openDecisions.question: What are the final performance limits?
openDecisions.evidence: benchmarkPlan.limitsStatus is TO_BE_DERIVED_FROM_MEASUREMENT. No implementation exists to measure.
openDecisions.implication: PST-PERF-003 already forbids asserting limits in advance; only the measured values remain open.

openDecisionPolicy.rule: No architectural, ownership, unit or data-flow decision may remain open at merge. Every such decision from revision 1.0.0 was resolved in 1.1.0 and moved to resolvedDecisions.

benchmarkPlan.referenceBaseline: POST /portfolio/live-refresh executes one batch request per 60s refresh cycle with zero per-leg, zero per-cell and zero option-chain requests. The stress endpoint must not regress from that shape.

temporalModel.freezeRule: read and copy every market input into the snapshot before the first scenario calculation
temporalModel.thresholdVisibility: every threshold must be declared and reported; a hidden threshold is a contract violation
temporalModel.overlayRule: an overlay edit invalidates the run and requires a rerun; it never triggers an in-place market read
temporalModel.existingOwnerEvidence: The reused owners already carry most of this. The backend underlying resolver publishes source, updatedAt, isStale, quoteAgeMs and quoteFreshness per symbol; readOptionLivePayloadForPortfolio publishes greeksStale, quoteStale and greeksUnavailableReason per option; the VIX family snapshot publishes updatedAt and a partial flag; the beta store publishes asOfDate and computeBetaAgeDays. PST-TEMPORAL-004 is therefore largely a PROPAGATION requirement, not a new measurement one.
requiredTests: SPY is not reread part-way through the matrix
quotes are not refetched per scenario
Actual and Proposed carry identical timestamps
adding an overlay leg triggers no new market read
a snapshot without snapshotStartedAt is rejected
an input without asOf is rejected
maxCrossInputSkewMs is computed
